title: framework-guide
content:
# SPECTION Framework Guide

## Purpose and audience

SPECTION helps developers, architects, students and teams build software that solves validated user problems. It combines specification-driven development, agent harnesses and evidence-based engineering. It supports both conventional applications and products integrating AI; an LLM is not a mandatory application dependency.

## How the framework works

| Stage | Input | Deliverable | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discover | Business idea, interviews | Product Brief, success measures | Stakeholder validates problem and scope |
| Specify | Reviewed brief | PRD, RF/RNF IDs, acceptance criteria | Requirements reviewed and testable |
| Architect | Requirements | HLD, ADRs, LLD | Trade-offs and risks reviewed |
| Plan | Approved feature | Feature spec, plan, tasks | Dependencies and verification defined |
| Build | Bounded tasks | Code and tests | Reviewable changes; actual checks |
| Verify | Implementation | Traceability and test evidence | Acceptance, security and human review |
| Release | Reviewed increment | Release notes, rollback, monitoring | Explicit production approval |
| Evolve | Feedback and incidents | Updated specs and prioritized tasks | Change impact reviewed |

This is iterative, not a mandatory waterfall. Revisit specifications when evidence changes. Small changes can use lightweight documents; risky changes require deeper analysis.

## Harness engineering

The harness is the context and control system around the AI model: AGENTS.md, approved specs, skills, tools, permission boundaries and feedback from tests. Feedforward guidance informs the agent before implementation; feedback checks detect issues afterward. Neither automatically proves correctness. Tool permissions must be enforced outside the model, not just requested in prompts.

## Roles

The product owner validates value and scope; the developer owns implementation and evidence; architects review design trade-offs; security/privacy specialists assess material risk; a responsible human authorizes production. AI assists these roles, never substitutes for accountability.

## Start

Use [SPECTION Kit](../kit/README.md), the [developer workflow](developer-guide.md), and the [reference architecture](../kit/docs/architecture.md). See [responsible development](responsible-development.md) for safeguards.

title: developer-guide
content:
# Developer Guide - Accelerate software delivery with SPECTION

## Installation and first project

Install Git and Python 3.10+. From a terminal:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/alexsandsouza/spection.git
cd spection
python kit/spection.py init my-app
python kit/spection.py feature my-app account-login
python kit/spection.py doctor my-app
python kit/spection.py check my-app
```

No API key is required by the CLI. It generates local documents, not application code. Open my-app in your editor and supply AGENTS.md plus relevant project files to your chosen coding assistant. Skills live in the SPECTION repository; provide the relevant SKILL.md explicitly if your agent does not discover them.

## Practical scenario: appointment booking

1. **Discover:** Interview reception staff and customers; record appointment conflicts and expected outcomes in the Product Brief.
2. **Specify:** RF-001: a customer requests an available slot. RF-002: overlapping bookings are rejected. RNF-001: define measurable response-time target with stakeholders.
3. **Architect:** HLD: browser, API, transactional database. ADR: choose database constraints rather than relying on client-side checks. LLD: define booking endpoint, authorization, conflict response and transaction behavior.
4. **Plan:** FEAT-001 links RF-001/RF-002; AC-001 accepts an available slot; AC-002 rejects concurrent conflicts; TASK-001 implements data constraint; TASK-002 tests concurrency.
5. **Build:** Ask the agent for a minimal patch on a branch. Review code and run unit/integration tests with the chosen stack.
6. **Verify:** Record command, environment, actual result and commit. Mark criteria verified only when evidence supports them.
7. **Release:** review privacy, backup, migration, rollback and monitoring. Obtain explicit approval.

## Example prompt to use with your agent

> Read AGENTS.md, docs/prd.md, docs/hld.md, docs/lld.md and the active feature spec. Restate the goal, assumptions and acceptance criteria. Propose the smallest implementation plan with requirement IDs, tests and security considerations. Do not edit unrelated files or deploy. After implementation, run applicable checks and report exact results, remaining risks and documentation changes.

## How SPECTION can accelerate work

- Reduce repeated context setup using stable, versioned specifications and skills.
- Reduce rework by resolving ambiguity before implementation.
- Split work into small parallelizable tasks only after dependencies are known.
- Generate drafts, test cases and review checklists; humans validate outputs.
- Automate repeatable checks in CI and reuse architectural decisions.

Measure before claiming improvement: lead time from accepted requirement to release, review/rework hours, escaped defects, change failure rate, deployment frequency and cost per delivered feature. Compare equivalent work against a baseline. There is no guaranteed speedup.

## Existing projects

Start in a separate directory; inventory current interfaces, tests, dependencies and architecture. Copy only reviewed templates, preserve existing conventions, and introduce SPECTION incrementally around one feature. Never overwrite existing files blindly.

title: ethical-use
content:
# Ethical and Responsible Use

SPECTION supports accountable software engineering, not unchecked automation. These guidelines supplement, and do not restrict, the MIT license.

## Principles
- Human accountability: identify a responsible owner; review consequential decisions and provide recourse.
- Privacy: minimize data, avoid secrets in prompts and logs, review provider retention and transfers.
- Fairness and accessibility: evaluate foreseeable harms, representative cases and inclusive user journeys.
- Transparency: disclose material AI use and limitations; do not misrepresent generated content or test evidence.
- Security: enforce least privilege outside the model, validate outputs and require approval for high-impact tool actions.
- Intellectual property: review licensing and attribution of generated and third-party material.
- Sustainability: measure cost, latency, energy-relevant resource use and choose proportionate solutions.

## Release checklist
- [ ] Requirements and acceptance criteria reviewed.
- [ ] Threat model and privacy assessment reviewed.
- [ ] Applicable tests executed with evidence.
- [ ] Model evaluations and misuse cases reviewed when AI is integrated.
- [ ] Accessibility, fairness and human escalation considered.
- [ ] Rollback, monitoring, incident owner and release approval recorded.

Report vulnerabilities privately when possible; avoid posting secrets or personal data in public issues. The framework is not a certification or legal guarantee. See [responsible development](responsible-development.md) and [security guidance](../kit/docs/security-ethics.md).

title: architecture
content:
# SPECTION Architecture Reference

This diagram is a proposed **reference architecture**, not a requirement for every application. AI gateway, agents and vector search are optional.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  A["SPECTION SDD: Brief · PRD · HLD · LLD · ADR"] --> B["Application / API: UX · Auth · Business Logic"]
  B --> C["Optional AI Gateway: Model routing · Policy · Limits · Cost"]
  C --> D["Models / Providers"]
  C --> E["Agents · Tools · MCP"]
  C --> F["Retrieval / RAG · Vector stores"]
  E --> G["Approved services / databases"]
  F --> G
  H["Governance: Privacy · Threat modeling · Evals · Guardrails · Monitoring · Human approval"] -. applies to .-> A
  H -. applies to .-> B
  H -. applies to .-> C
  H -. applies to .-> E
```

## Layers

| Layer | Responsibility | Optional? |
|---|---|---|
| SDD and review | traceability, specs, architecture decisions, approval | No |
| Application | user experience, business rules, authentication, access control | Depends on system |
| AI Gateway | model routing, quotas, logging hygiene, rate limiting | Yes |
| Models and agents | generation, planning, retrieval, supervised tools | Yes |
| Data | SQL/NoSQL/vector stores selected by real access patterns | Yes |
| Governance | privacy, security, evaluation and accountability | No |

## Architecture decision process

First document business and quality requirements, then compare alternatives in an ADR. Evaluate latency, availability, security, lock-in, accessibility, cost and operational complexity. Do not select vector databases, cloud providers or agents solely because they are popular.

## AI system considerations

Apply least privilege to tools, treat retrieved and model-generated data as untrusted, constrain network and filesystem access, separate user instructions from retrieved documents, log safely and require explicit approval for external side effects.

## Relationship to HLD and LLD

HLD answers what services exist and how they communicate; LLD defines endpoint contracts, data schema, error cases and implementation rules; ADR records why design choices were made.

title: README
content:
# SPECTION Kit

**Open, vendor-neutral toolkit for responsible AI-guided software delivery.**

SPECTION Kit is the practical, executable companion to the SPECTION framework. It is an original implementation, not a fork or replacement of GitHub Spec Kit.

## What is included

- A minimal Python standard-library CLI (`kit/spection.py`)
- Reusable product, architecture and feature templates
- Guided workflow descriptions for new projects, features, fixes and releases
- Policy templates for security, ethical review and AI evaluation
- Repository checks and local unit tests
- Documentation in English and Portuguese

## Quickstart

Requirements: Python 3.10 or newer. No API keys or paid services required.

Clone this repository and run:

```bash
python kit/spection.py init my-project
python kit/spection.py doctor my-project
python kit/spection.py feature my-project user-registration
python kit/spection.py check my-project
```

Commands create files locally; no AI API is called and nothing is deployed. The CLI refuses to overwrite existing files and rejects unsafe path names. Review generated templates before giving them to an AI agent.

## Workflow

1. **Discover:** define problem, users, outcomes and exclusions.
2. **Specify:** record RF/RNF requirements and testable acceptance criteria.
3. **Architect:** draft HLD and LLD with ADRs for trade-offs.
4. **Plan:** split feature work into traceable, small tasks.
5. **Build:** develop with an AI agent constrained by AGENTS.md.
6. **Verify:** execute tests, review security and record evidence.
7. **Release:** obtain human approval, document rollback and monitor.

In production-facing workflows, human review is mandatory.

## Important distinctions

- **SPECTION Framework:** methodology and documentation (root `docs/`, `.agents/skills/`).
- **SPECTION Kit:** bootstrap and validation tooling plus repeatable workflows (`kit/`).
- **GitHub Spec Kit:** separate upstream project. SPECTION does not claim compatibility with Spec Kit commands or extensions.

## Documentation

- [User guide](docs/user-guide.md)
- [Architecture diagram](docs/architecture.md)
- [Security, privacy and ethics](docs/security-ethics.md)
- [Workflow catalog](workflows/README.md)
- [Glossary](../GLOSSARY.md)

## Scope

Version 0.2 foundation is an offline CLI and templates. It is **not** a web application, an AI model, a guaranteed compliance audit or a substitute for secure software review.

title: README
content:
# SPECTION Examples

These are illustrative specification exercises, not deployed applications.

## 1. Booking API (conventional software)
Read the [worked example](../docs/developer-guide.md). Start with RF-001 booking creation and RF-002 conflict prevention. Design a transaction boundary and test simultaneous requests. Record results in the traceability matrix.

## 2. AI document assistant
Specify approved sources, permissions and citations. Compare deterministic search with RAG in an ADR. Define refusal when no evidence exists, test prompt injection and unauthorized retrieval, and measure quality, p95 latency and cost. Use the [AI integration workflow](../kit/workflows/ai-integration.md) and [evaluation template](../kit/docs/model-evaluation.md).

## 3. Existing application
Choose one small change, inventory current behavior, write an acceptance test and feature spec, then implement a minimal patch. Follow the [bug-fix workflow](../kit/workflows/bug-fix.md).

No example claims executed tests or production readiness.

title: README.pt-BR
content:
# SPECTION - Guia em português

SPECTION é um framework aberto de Engenharia de Software Guiada por IA. Seu objetivo é ajudar a desenvolver aplicações úteis, seguras, eficientes, éticas e responsáveis, com especificações versionadas e supervisão humana.

## Como funciona

Ideia → Product Brief → requisitos (PRD) → arquitetura (HLD/LLD/ADR) → especificação da funcionalidade → plano e tarefas → implementação → testes e revisão → entrega e evolução. O processo é iterativo: mudanças de requisito voltam à especificação.

## Como começar

Clone o repositório, instale Python 3.10+ e execute:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/alexsandsouza/spection.git
cd spection
python kit/spection.py init minha-app
python kit/spection.py feature minha-app cadastro
python kit/spection.py doctor minha-app
python kit/spection.py check minha-app
```

Preencha o Product Brief e os requisitos. Abra o projeto no editor e informe ao agente os documentos relevantes e AGENTS.md. Solicite primeiro um plano, depois código em pequenas mudanças e testes reais. Revise a saída, registre evidências e autorize a publicação explicitamente.

## Por que acelera?

Documentos e skills reduzem a repetição de contexto; critérios de aceitação reduzem ambiguidades; tarefas pequenas facilitam revisão; automação ajuda a detectar problemas. Meça tempo de entrega, retrabalho, defeitos e custo antes de afirmar ganhos.

## Segurança e responsabilidade

Não envie segredos ou dados pessoais para modelos sem autorização e controles adequados. Revise permissões, riscos, dependências, acessibilidade, privacidade e impactos. Se a aplicação usa IA, avalie qualidade, latência, custo, prompt injection e limites de ferramentas. O framework não garante conformidade nem substitui avaliação especializada.

## Documentação

- [Funcionamento](framework-guide.md)
- [Guia prático com exemplo](developer-guide.md)
- [Desenvolvimento responsável](responsible-development.md)
- [Arquitetura de IA](../kit/docs/architecture.md)
- [Direitos autorais](../COPYRIGHT.md)
- [Licença MIT](../LICENSE)

## Original work and inspiration

SPECTION is an independently organized framework drawing on established software engineering practices, Spec-Driven Development and Harness Engineering. GitHub Spec Kit is a separate project and a conceptual reference; SPECTION is not an official GitHub product, fork or endorsed implementation.

## Third-party material

Respect the licenses and attribution requirements of dependencies, examples, images, documentation and code. Do not assume the MIT license of this repository relicenses third-party material. Record component name, source, license, version and required notices when incorporating third-party assets. Do not copy proprietary course slides, screenshots or protected text into the project without appropriate permission.

## Contributions and AI-assisted work

Contributors must have the right to submit their contributions under MIT. Review AI-generated material for originality, licensing, confidential information and potential infringement before submission. Do not include secrets or personal data. Attribution does not substitute for permission where it is required.

## Name and marks

The MIT license does not by itself establish trademark rights or grant rights to third-party names and logos. SPECTION is the project name; no trademark registration or exclusive rights are asserted here. Verify name availability before commercial branding.

## Reporting concerns

Report suspected infringement or attribution errors through the repository's issue tracker without publishing sensitive material. Maintainers should investigate, correct notices or remove material as appropriate.

This document is project guidance; the LICENSE file controls the MIT license terms.

title: model-evaluation
content:
# Model & Agent Evaluation Plan

## Evaluation profile

- User journey and business outcome:
- Model / version / provider:
- Prompt / tool configuration:
- Data classification / approval:
- Test dataset provenance:
- Date / execution environment:

## Metrics

| Dimension | Example measurement | Acceptance threshold | Actual evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Task quality | Task success rate on representative cases | Set before test | Pending |
| Safety | Allowed/disallowed behavior and prompt-injection tests | Set before test | Pending |
| Privacy | Sensitive data exposure cases | Set before test | Pending |
| Reliability | Repeated-run variance and tool failures | Set before test | Pending |
| Latency | p50 / p95 end-to-end response | Set before test | Pending |
| Cost | Cost per successful transaction | Set before test | Pending |
| Human experience | Satisfaction, accessibility and overrides | Set before test | Pending |

## Evaluation rules

Use representative, legally obtained datasets. Keep holdout examples. Test actual tool boundaries, not only text quality. Track failures and regressions. Do not say 'passed' unless there is a verifiable run identifier.

title: security-ethics
content:
# Security, Privacy & Responsible AI

SPECTION is a process aid, **not a certification or compliance guarantee**. Organizations must obtain expert legal and security review for their context.

## Threats to consider

- Prompt injection through user input, documents, search results and tool outputs
- Jailbreak attempts and unsafe model behavior
- Sensitive-information leakage via prompts, logs, embeddings, telemetry and responses
- Excessive agent authority, unintended tool invocation and privilege escalation
- Unsafe output consumption (SQL, shell commands, HTML, code, external URLs)
- Model supply-chain and dependency risks
- Poisoned retrieval content, manipulated vector indexes and misleading citations
- Denial-of-wallet, quotas, latency spikes and service failures

## Controls

1. Least privilege for users, models, agents and integrations.
2. Strict schema validation and output encoding at trust boundaries.
3. Credential handling via secret managers / environment; never commit secrets.
4. Human authorization for payments, data deletion, bulk modifications, messages and deployment.
5. Vendor/data-transfer review; minimize data sent to model providers.
6. Rate limits, budgets, retries, circuit breakers and incident response plans.
7. Meaningful eval sets covering misuse, multilingual inputs, false claims and regressions.
8. Record real evidence, model versions and uncertainties; avoid invented metrics.

## Ethical design review

Ask: Is the system accessible? Are users informed where AI is used? Are impacts on vulnerable groups assessed? Is automation reversible? Are harms observable and contestable? Is privacy respected?

## References

- [OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications](https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/)
- [OWASP Agentic AI](https://genai.owasp.org/)
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)
- [Brazilian LGPD official law text](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2015-2018/2018/lei/l13709.htm)

Standards evolve. Check the official sources and applicable jurisdiction before declaring compliance.
